source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
The source describes visible leaf symptoms farmers can use to recognize major nutrient deficiencies in pomelo trees. Nitrogen deficiency shows as overall pale yellowing of older leaves and reduced vigor and growth. Phosphorus deficiency is harder to see directly but is associated with dark, dull-green leaves, poor root development, and reduced flowering/fruiting, and the source notes phosphorus and calcium levels together influence flowering. Potassium deficiency shows first on older leaves as yellowing and scorching along the leaf margins, with leaves eventually becoming brittle and prone to premature drop; fruit from potassium-deficient trees also tends to be smaller with thinner juice content.

Correcting these deficiencies is done through balanced fertilizing - the source recommends applying NPK compound fertilizer (such as 15-15-15) together with urea on a regular schedule (see the fertilizing entry in the orange knowledge base, which follows the same general MAFF approach for citrus), rather than single-nutrient correction after visible symptoms appear, since by the time deficiency symptoms are visible on leaves, yield has often already been affected.
